questions.q:
Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

15 ÷ 80 - 34 + 10 × 8 = 102
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

Option 1) : 10, 80, ÷, -

Given equation is : 15 ÷ 80 - 34 + 10 × 8 = 102

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 15 - 10 ÷ 34 + 80 × 8 = 102

⇒ 15 - 10 ÷ 34 + 80 × 8 = 102

⇒ 15 - 0.29411 + 80 × 8 = 102

⇒ 15 - 0.29411 + 640 = 102

⇒ 655 - 0.29411 = 102

⇒ 654.7058 ≠ 102

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : 15, 34, -, ×

Given equation is : 15 ÷ 80 - 34 + 10 × 8 = 102

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 34 ÷ 80 × 15 + 10 - 8 = 102

⇒ 34 ÷ 80 × 15 + 10 - 8 = 102

⇒ 0.425 × 15 + 10 - 8 = 102

⇒ 6.375 + 10 - 8 = 102

⇒ 16.375 - 8 = 102

⇒ 8.375 ≠ 102

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : 34, 15, +, ÷

Given equation is : 15 ÷ 80 - 34 + 10 × 8 = 102

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 34 + 80 - 15 ÷ 10 × 8 = 102

⇒ 34 + 80 - 15 ÷ 10 × 8 = 102

⇒ 34 + 80 - 1.5 × 8 = 102

⇒ 34 + 80 - 12 = 102

⇒ 114 - 12 = 102

⇒ 102 = 102

LHS = RHS

Option 4) : 10, 34, ÷, ×

Given equation is : 15 ÷ 80 - 34 + 10 × 8 = 102

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 15 × 80 - 10 + 34 ÷ 8 = 102

⇒ 15 × 80 - 10 + 34 ÷ 8 = 102

⇒ 15 × 80 - 10 + 4.25 = 102

⇒ 1200 - 10 + 4.25 = 102

⇒ 1204.25 - 10 = 102

⇒ 1194.25 ≠ 102

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "34, 15, +, ÷".

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to establish additional courts for better administration of laws made by it?

The correct answer is Article 247.

• The Indian Constitution provides for a three-tier judiciary system, comprising the Supreme Court, High Courts, and subordinate courts.

• The Parliament has the power to establish additional courts to deal with specific kinds of cases or to cater to the needs of a particular region or community.

• Article 247 of the Constitution empowers the Parliament to establish such courts for the better administration of laws made by it.

• This includes the power to create tribunals, which are specialized bodies that adjudicate on specific matters such as taxation, labor disputes, and environmental issues.

Additional Information

• Article 246 deals with the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States.

• It specifies that Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on matters listed in the Union List, while the State Legislatures have exclusive power to make laws on matters listed in the State List.

• Both the Union and the State Legislatures can make laws on matters listed in the Concurrent List.

• Article 248 provides for the residuary powers of legislation, i.e., the power to make laws on any matter not enumerated in the three lists.

• This power is vested in Parliament, subject to the provisions of the Constitution.

• Article 253 empowers the Parliament to make laws for implementing any international agreement, treaty, or convention.

• This power is necessary to fulfill India's obligations under international law and to ensure uniformity in the implementation of such agreements across the country.

questions.q: 10 women take 16 days to complete a work which can be completed by 6 men in 8 days. 12 men started working and after 2 days 6 men left, and 5 women joined them. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Efficiency Ratio (W:M) ⇒ 10W × 16 : 6M × 8 ⇒ 160 : 48 ⇒ 10 : 3 (W=3, M=10).

Total Work = 10 × 3 × 16 = 480 units.

Work done by 12 men in 2 days = 12 × 10 × 2 = 240 units.

Remaining Work = 480 − 240 = 240 units.

New Efficiency (6M + 5W) = (6 × 10) + (5 × 3) = 75 units/day.

Total time = 2 + (240 ÷ 75) = 2 + 16/5 = 26/5 days.

∴ The correct answer is 26/5 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Work completed by 10 women in 16 days.

Work completed by 6 men in 8 days.

Initial workforce: 12 men for 2 days.

New workforce: 6 men (12 − 6) and 5 women.

Formula Used:

Total Work = Number of persons × Efficiency × Time



Calculations:

⇒ 10 Women × 16 days = 6 Men × 8 days

⇒ 160W = 48M ⇒ 10W = 3M ⇒ M/W = 10/3

⇒ Efficiency of 1 Man (M) = 10 units, 1 Woman (W) = 3 units

⇒ Total Work = 48 × 10 = 480 units

⇒ Work done in first 2 days = 12M × 2 = 12 × 10 × 2 = 240 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 480 − 240 = 240 units

⇒ Efficiency of new group (6M + 5W) = 6(10) + 5(3) = 60 + 15 = 75 units/day

⇒ Time for remaining work = 240 ÷ 75 = 16/5 days

⇒ Total time taken = 2 + 16/5 = 26/5 days

∴ The correct answer is 26/5 days.

Additional Information

Work-Efficiency Relationship

Total work is the product of number of workers, their efficiency, and the time taken (Work = M × E × D). For the same work, (M₁D₁E₁) = (M₂D₂E₂).

Combined Efficiency

When different types of workers (men, women, children) work together, their net efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies multiplied by their respective counts.

Fractional Days

If work is not finished in a whole number of days, the time is expressed as (Total Work Done) / (Work done per day), often leading to improper fractions like 26/5.
